'''Ian Grote Stirling''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|OC|FRSC}} (September 26, 1941{{snd}}May 14, 2024)<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wenger |first=Dr Michael |title=The polar retrospective – Polar bear researcher Ian Stirling dies at 82 |url=https://polarjournal.ch/en/2024/05/21/the-polar-retrospective-polar-bear-researcher-ian-stirling-dies-at-82/ |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=Polarjournal |language=en-US}}</ref> was a research scientist with [[Environment and Climate Change Canada]] and an adjunct professor in the [[University of Alberta]] Department of Biological Sciences.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |date=2016 |title=Kenneth S. Norris Lifetime Achievement Award |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/mms.12294 |journal=Marine Mammal Science |language=en |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=10–12 |doi=10.1111/mms.12294 |bibcode=2016MMamS..32...10. |issn=0824-0469|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=CSE>{{cite web|url=http://www.councilscienceeditors.org:80/events/annualmeeting08/speakers.cfm |title=The Council of Science Editors (CSE) - 2007 Annual Meeting |website=Councilscienceeditors.org |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080403060552/http://www.councilscienceeditors.org/events/annualmeeting08/speakers.cfm |archivedate=April 3, 2008 }}</ref> His research has focused mostly on [[Arctic]] and [[Antarctic]] zoology and ecology, and he was one of the world's top authorities on [[polar bear]]s.<ref name=cbc>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca:80/news/background/polarbears/ |title=CBC News Indepth: Polar Bears |date=6 July 2004|website=Cbc.ca |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012114434/http://www.cbc.ca/news/background/polarbears/ |archivedate=October 12, 2007 }}</ref>

Stirling authored five non-technical books and more than 250 articles published in peer-reviewed science journals.<ref name=":0" /> Over the course of his career, and well into his retirement from [[Environment Canada]] in 2007, when he became a scientist emeritus, he wrote and spoke extensively about the danger posed to polar bears by [[global warming]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Post |first1=Eric |last2=Forchhammer |first2=Mads C. |last3=Bret-Harte |first3=M. Syndonia |last4=Callaghan |first4=Terry V. |last5=Christensen |first5=Torben R. |last6=Elberling |first6=Bo |last7=Fox |first7=Anthony D. |last8=Gilg |first8=Olivier |last9=Hik |first9=David S. |last10=Høye |first10=Toke T. |last11=Ims |first11=Rolf A. |last12=Jeppesen |first12=Erik |last13=Klein |first13=David R. |last14=Madsen |first14=Jesper |last15=McGuire |first15=A. David |date=2009-09-11 |title=Ecological Dynamics Across the Arctic Associated with Recent Climate Change |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1173113 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=325 |issue=5946 |pages=1355–1358 |doi=10.1126/science.1173113 |pmid=19745143 |bibcode=2009Sci...325.1355P |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Ian Stirling was born to Andrew and Margaret Stirling on September 26, 1941 in Zambia, where his father worked as a mining engineer. They returned to Canada after the Second World War, settling in the mining town of [[Kimberley, British Columbia]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Remembering the life of Ian STIRLING |url=https://vancouversunandprovince.remembering.ca/obituary/ian-stirling-1089813802/ |access-date=2024-05-24 |website=vancouversunandprovince.remembering.ca |language=en}}</ref> He completed his B.Sc. at the [[University of British Columbia]] (UBC) in 1963, and his M.Sc. in zoology at UBC in 1965, where he met his spouse, Stella.<ref name=":2" />

For his M.Sc. thesis, Stirling studied captive [[Dendragapus fuliginosus|blue grouse]] under James F. Bendell.<ref>{{cite thesis|title=Studies of the holding, behaviour and nutrition of captive blue grouse|first=Stirling, Ian|last=Grote|date=1 January 1965|publisher=University of British Columbia |doi=10.14288/1.0302522|hdl = 2429/37452}}</ref> In 1968, Stirling received his doctorate from the [[University of Canterbury|University of Canterbury, New Zealand]] having done his field work on the [[Weddell seal]] from [[Scott Base]] in [[Antarctica]], followed by post-doctoral research on [[Brown fur seal|South Australian fur seals]] at the [[University of Adelaide]] in Australia.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Stirling |first=Ian |year=1968 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Population ecology of the Weddell seal (Leptonychotes weddelli) in McMurdo Sound, Antarctica |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/6646 |doi=10.26021/6015 |url=https://ir.canterbury.ac.nz/handle/10092/6646}}</ref> His three children were born in New Zealand, Australia and Canada, respectively.<ref name=":2" />

==Career==
From 1970 to 2007, Stirling was employed as a research scientist for the [[Canadian Wildlife Service]].<ref name=":0" /> His research focussed on polar bear biology and ecology, with his most notable work being  a long-term study of polar bears in western [[Hudson Bay]] near [[Churchill, Manitoba]]. He was among the first to draw attention to the potential impacts of [[climate change]] on polar bears.<ref>{{cite journal |last1 = Stirling |first1 = Ian |last2 = Derocher |first2 = Andrew E. |date = 1993 |title = Possible impacts of climatic warming on polar bears |url = http://hdl.handle.net/10515/sy5q23r36 |journal = Arctic |publisher = Arctic Institute of North America |volume = 46 |issue = 3 |pages = 240–245 |doi = 10.14430/arctic1348|doi-access = free }}</ref> He was also an adjunct professor at the [[University of Alberta]] for more than 30 years, after settling in Edmonton in 1972.<ref name=":2" /> Stirling retired in 2007.

Stirling has served as a member of the Committee of Scientific Advisors of the [[Marine Mammal Commission]], and he was the first Canadian to be elected president of the [[Society for Marine Mammalogy]].<ref name=star>{{cite web|url=http://www.thestar.com:80/ArcticInPeril/article/279817 |title=TheStar.com - Arctic In Peril - Polar bear population on thin ice |date=26 November 2007 |website=Thestar.com |url-status=unfit |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080403023622/http://www.thestar.com/ArcticInPeril/article/279817 |archivedate=April 3, 2008 }}</ref> He was a long-standing member of the [[IUCN]] [[Polar Bear Specialist Group]] and was also a scientific advisor to [[Polar Bears International]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Scientist Ian Stirling Receives Ice Bear Lifetime Achievement Award {{!}} Polar Bears International |url=https://polarbearsinternational.org/news-media/articles/scientist-ian-stirling-ice-bear-lifetime-achievement-award/ |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=polarbearsinternational.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Death ==

Stirling was diagnosed with [[lymphoma]] in 2019.  The illness advanced to leukemia in 2023 and he died of effects of cancer in 2024, at age 82.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ian Stirling Obit|url=https://polarbearscience.com/2024/05/19/ian-stirling-grandfather-of-polar-bear-biologists-dead-at-83/ |access-date=May 26, 2024 |publisher=polarbearscience.com}}</ref>

*Stirling I (1997) The importance of polynyas, ice edges, and leads to marine mammals and birds. ''Journal of Marine Systems'' 10, 9–21.
*Stirling I, Lunn NJ, Iacozza J (1999) Long-term trends in the population ecology of polar bears in western Hudson Bay in relation to climatic change. ''Arctic'' 52, 294–306.
*Stirling I, Parkinson CL (2006) Possible effects of climate warming on selected populations of polar bears (''Ursus maritimus'') in the Canadian Arctic. ''Arctic'' 59, 261–275.
*Stirling I, Derocher AE (2012) Effects of climate warming on polar bears: a review of the evidence. ''Global Change Biology'' 18, 2694–2706. {{doi|10.1111/j.1365-2486.2012.02753.x}}
